title: Hollow and Veil
premise: Mara Dravenmoor, a mercenary bound by oath to the silent god Veyl, discovers that the god's silence and the extinguished stars are one catastrophe: a memory-eating entity called the Hollow has worn King Aldric's crown for years, devouring the kingdom's past to unmake its wards. Guided by Sera, a ward-singer who remembers too much, and Tamsin, an orphan pickpocket who becomes their found family, Mara traces the Hollow's roots to a bargain their own grandmother struck generations ago. In the throne room beneath a starless sky, Mara learns that binding the Hollow requires surrendering every memory of everyone they love—and chooses instead to share the burden, splitting it among all who willingly remember. The stars relight, Aldric dies free, and Mara, half-erased but held together by found family, begins the slow work of remembering who they were.
about_author: Ines Iversen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters no one claimed, an experience that taught her how much of a life lives in what others choose to keep. She writes fantasy about inheritance, obligation, and the families we build when blood runs out.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Smuggling a cargo through Thornfell, Mara notices the border wards flickering as the stars vanish overhead, and their oath-mark to the silent god Veyl burns cold for the first time in years. They reach the waystation to find their handler dead, his memories visibly leaking from him like smoke. Emotional beat: dread—the invisible life Mara built is ending, and they know it.

chapters.title: What the Wards Were Made Of
chapters.summary: POV Sera. Ward-singer Sera Ilyich is arrested for failing to maintain the border wards until she proves they weren't broken—they were eaten. She escapes with evidence that the wards were woven from recorded royal memory, and that something has been consuming them for years. Emotional beat: righteous fury hardening into purpose; she will find the thief even if the court calls her mad.

chapters.title: A Thief Named Tamsin
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. Eleven-year-old pickpocket Tamsin lifts Mara's purse in the border town of Grayhollow and finds a coin that shouldn't exist: minted with a king's face no one can remember. Hunted by gray-eyed strangers who forget people mid-sentence, she flees to the only adult who looked at her twice. Emotional beat: wary hope—two loners forced into alliance.

chapters.title: The Road Through Thornfell
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Fleeing Grayhollow together, Mara teaches Sera and Tamsin the smuggler roads while the Hollow's agents close in; each skirmish costs someone a memory, and Mara realizes their own childhood is full of holes they'd never questioned. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness—the trio becomes a unit around a campfire, sharing invented stories to replace stolen ones.

chapters.title: Letters From a Silent God
chapters.summary: POV Sera. In a ruined mountain shrine, Sera deciphers Veyl's last messages: the god didn't abandon the world—it went silent trying to hold the Hollow back, and Mara's oath-mark is a key it hid inside a mortal. Mara rages at being used as a lockbox. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into resolve; faith rebuilt on choice rather than command.

chapters.title: The Court That Forgot Its King
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. Infiltrating the capital disguised as a beggar child, Tamsin discovers the courtiers cannot describe the king beyond 'he rules,' and the crown itself hums with hunger. She steals a fragment of royal memory from the treasury and barely escapes, leaving a decoy behind. Emotional beat: terror transformed into pride—the smallest member saves them all.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Following the memory fragment to a sealed family vault, Mara learns the truth: their grandmother helped bind the Hollow into the crown generations ago, paying with her descendants' memories as collateral. Mara's erased childhood was the price already collected. Emotional beat: grief and inheritance—Mara must decide whether to honor a debt they never agreed to.

chapters.title: Everything We Chose to Keep
chapters.summary: POV Sera. As the Hollow's hunger accelerates and whole villages forget themselves, Sera proposes heresy: instead of one sacrifice, thousands of willing rememberers could each carry a sliver of the burden. The trio gathers allies—smugglers, ward-singers, orphans—to swear the shared oath before the last star-memory gutters out. Emotional beat: found family made literal, a covenant chosen over blood.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing the Crown
chapters.summary: POV Mara. In the starless throne room, Mara confronts the Hollow wearing King Aldric, who surfaces just long enough to beg for death. The Hollow offers Mara a trade: their grandmother's debt forgiven if they surrender Sera and Tamsin's memories instead. Mara refuses and begins the unbinding as the Hollow tears at everything they are. Emotional beat: the climax—love weaponized against erasure.

chapters.title: Half-Remembered, Whole
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. The shared oath holds: hundreds carry slivers of the burden, the stars relight, and Aldric dies a man rather than a vessel. Tamsin, now Mara's declared heir in the new order of Rememberers, guides a hollowed-out Mara through relearning their own name, their loves, their laugh. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—memory lost is mourned, but memory chosen, kept together, endures.
